holes_found.description: Cross-WIN consistency: WIN-023 is also currently classified Unfalsifiable in data/wins.json (verdict='Unfalsifiable', SAA formation ~950 AD paired with Revelation 20 'Satan's little season'). The detail_evidence carve-out example lists 'other Unfalsifiable WINs in this cluster, e.g., WIN-032' and computes '67/71 = 94.4% if WIN-031 and 032 are carved out.' The 'e.g.' framing implies non-exhaustive listing, but the arithmetic is exhaustive at exactly 2 carve-outs. A dome defender comparing our data/wins.json:verdict distribution ({Refuted 12, Self-Contradicted 20, Misleading 16, Std Model 18, Not Demonstrated 3, Unfalsifiable 3}) to the paragraph can pivot: 'You have three Unfalsifiable WINs (023, 031, 032) but you selectively carve out only two, and the specific arithmetic 67/71 assumes exactly that selection. Why is WIN-023 exempt? Either your carve-out criterion is inconsistent, or your arithmetic silently prefers the smaller impact.' The full three-WIN carve-out would be 66/70 = 94.286% ≈ 94.3% — still essentially unchanged from 94.5%, so the analytical point survives, but the arithmetic disagreement invites the challenge. WIN-023 is arguably a hybrid case (real paleomagnetic observation wrapped in theological interpretation), which could justify separate treatment, but the current text doesn't distinguish it.
holes_found.recommendation: Two clean fixes: (a) explicitly acknowledge WIN-023 as a hybrid case in a short parenthetical ('WIN-023 pairs an empirical observation with a theological reading and is a distinct sub-category; carving it out too would yield 66/70 = 94.3%, an even smaller move'), OR (b) expand the arithmetic to the full three-WIN carve-out: '(66/70 = 94.3% if all three currently-Unfalsifiable WINs are carved out).' Option (a) is preferable because it preserves the 'pure theological cross-reference' analytical category. Neither fix requires touching finding or tldr text — the issue is only in detail_evidence §3.

holes_found.description: Citation attribution loose for the cognitive-universals archetype claim. The c9 patch added 'convergence at this level of abstraction reflects a cognitive-universals archetype (Boyer 2001; Lakoff & Johnson 1980 vertical/central metaphor)'. Both citations are real works but neither is the canonical scholarly attribution for the axis-mundi-as-archetype claim. Pascal Boyer's 'Religion Explained' (2001, Basic Books) develops the counterintuitive-concepts / minimally-counterintuitive framework for why religious concepts spread — it is not primarily about axis-mundi topology and does not, to my knowledge, discuss the sacred-mountain-at-center pattern by name. Lakoff & Johnson's 'Metaphors We Live By' (1980, University of Chicago Press) analyzes orientational metaphors (UP=GOOD, CENTER=IMPORTANT) as embodied conceptual structures — real support for why 'center' is cognitively salient, but not itself a claim about cosmological archetypes. The primary scholarly attribution for the axis mundi as a cross-cultural archetype is Mircea Eliade — specifically 'The Sacred and the Profane' (1959, Harcourt) or 'Cosmos and History: The Myth of the Eternal Return' (1954, Princeton). A dome defender who checks the bibliography can pivot: 'You cited Boyer and Lakoff-Johnson for the axis-mundi archetype claim, but neither of those works develops it — you gestured at the cognitive-science shelf without pulling the right book. Your underlying concept is right but your citations are hand-waves.'
holes_found.recommendation: Add Eliade as the primary axis-mundi source and demote Boyer / Lakoff-Johnson to supporting cognitive-basis references: 'convergence at this level of abstraction reflects the axis mundi archetype documented cross-culturally by Eliade (1959, The Sacred and the Profane) — a cognitive-universals pattern (Boyer 2001; Lakoff & Johnson 1980 for the embodied-metaphor basis of CENTER=IMPORTANT) rather than corroboration of any specific ontological content.' Eliade is the canonical citation any comparative-religion reviewer expects to see; adding it costs one clause and preempts the citation-quality challenge.

kernel_of_truth.description: The six-text convergence on 'cosmic mountain in the north' is a real, well-attested Ancient Near East tradition documented in (data/wins.json:WIN-031.detail_evidence, paragraph 2) as the Zaphon-Zion typology — Isaiah 14:13 places the mount of assembly 'in the sides of the north', Psalm 48:2 identifies Mount Zion with that same mount, Job 26:7 and 37:22 and Ezekiel 1:4 use directional-north imagery for divine presence, and 1 Enoch 17-18 fills in the visionary geography. kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The convergence is retrodictive (texts predate the model by ~2-3 millennia per detail_evidence §1) so cannot be a confirmed prediction; the axis-mundi archetype fits mutually contradictory cosmologies (Hindu Meru at r=0 flat-disc OR at north-pole-of-sphere; Norse Yggdrasil vertical three-tier; Islamic Qaf perimeter — cited in detail_evidence §2) so has zero discriminating power; and the WIN is counted in the dome's 69-confirmed / 94.5%-accuracy scorecard (verified in raw-text/02b-wins-V51-win064.txt — 'Confirmed Wins (69)') alongside empirically tested claims like WIN-029 Schumann frequency, pricing theological convergence at par with data-grounded physics.

deeper_analysis: This is a c10 re-review triggered by drift-audit.json (rank-1 candidate, +11.04% detail_evidence drift). The drift is traceable to a single commit (99128197, 2026-07-25) which self-applied the three c9 holes. Verifying closure: hole 0 (WIN-034 stale reference) is fixed — WIN-034 no longer named and verdict correctly reflects data/wins.json:WIN-034.verdict='Self-Contradicted'; hole 1 (topological-convergence pivot) is addressed with a new paragraph explicitly acknowledging Puranic Hindu Meru and Mesopotamian E-kur share flat-disc-with-central-mountain topology and framing the response via cognitive-universals archetype; hole 2 (provenance qualifiers) is addressed with 'as of 2026-05-08 dome scorecard capture; see raw-text/02b-wins-V51-win064.txt' and a monitor.py commit-hash + date qualifier. All three fixes are substantive and closed. New issues introduced or surfaced by the patch: (a) WIN-023 remains Unfalsifiable but is omitted from the two-WIN carve-out arithmetic — a cross-WIN inconsistency the c9 patch did not survey; (b) the provenance qualifier for monitor.py is nested inside a parenthetical that already mentions commit 8e4bf9b, producing textual redundancy; (c) the cognitive-universals citations (Boyer 2001, Lakoff & Johnson 1980) are gesturing citations — the canonical axis-mundi archetype source is Eliade (1959) and the current attribution invites a citation-quality challenge. All three new holes are minor (cosmetic or peripheral), the verdict Unfalsifiable stands unchanged, and the analytical core is stronger than at c9. The advocate-mode selective-epistemology pivot is a genuine open flank the c9 patch did not close and is the strongest recommendation for the next content edit; the three minor-hole fixes are cheap polish. No verdict change and no major rewrite indicated.
